risks.risk: Pump may not hold pressure or may have a leaking valve/connector (common issue not visible from a single photo).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video inflating a ball/tire to a target pressure and holding it for 5–10 minutes (or a pressure test reading if available).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially not holding pressure / needs repair (worst case: treat as not reliably working).

risks.risk: Wrong nozzle/connector type for the buyer’s intended use (ball, bicycle valve, inflatable mattress, etc.).
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of all included nozzles/adapters and a photo showing the exact valve connection end.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as generic/possibly missing the correct adapter (worst case: limited compatibility).

risks.risk: Condition issues like bent parts, worn seals, or internal damage that won’t show clearly in the photo.
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of the pump head/valve area and the connector end, plus a video showing pumping action (no unusual noise/knocking).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as used with unknown internal condition (worst case: may need servicing).

risks.risk: Seller may be overstating 'never opened' / 'low mileage'—not verifiable remotely.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of any serial/label and confirmation of whether seals show tampering; ideally a video of the pump being opened only if the buyer agrees (or show valve assembly without disassembly).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown history (worst case: treat as higher wear).

proof_requests: Short video: inflate an item (ball or inflatable) from empty to a clear target, then show it holding for 5–10 minutes.
Close-up photos of the pump head/valve and the connector/nozzle end (showing the exact valve type).
Photos of any included adapters/nozzles (if any) laid out clearly.
Photo of any label/serial/brand/model on the pump body (if present).
